summary: Hisao Takahashi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Taisho University, including under Ryukai Mano in 1979. He held posts at Taisho University as an assistant (~1974–1982), lecturer (~1987–1996), and professor (~1999–2015).

Hisashi Matsumura is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. His career includes an attested post at the Australian National University in 1982 and an assistant professorship at Kobe Shinwa University attested in 1996.

Hisashi Sato (1913–2008) worked in Tibetology, history, and archaeology. After studying at Kyoto University (~1933–1936), he was a professor there (1968), at Komazawa University, and at Toyo University, and held a post at Bukkyo University (~1976–1986).

Hisataka Ishida specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Akira Saito, Hiroshi Marui, Yoichi Fukuda, Masahiro Inami, and Helmut Krasser, earning a doctorate from the University of Vienna by 2011. He was a lecturer at Aichi Gakuin University in 2015.

Hisatake Kato (1937–2020) was a philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1957–1961). He held posts at Yamagata University (~1972–1979), Tohoku University (~1980–1992), the University of Tokyo (~1999–2001), Tottori University of Environmental Studies (~2001–2007), and the University of Human Arts and Sciences (~2007–2011).

Hitoshi Inui is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Kanjin Horiuchi. He served as a lecturer at the Research Institute of Esoteric Buddhist Culture (attested 1992) and was a professor at Koyasan University (attested 2015).

Hitoshi Kato specializes in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He held positions at Otani University, Osaka University of Foreign Studies (attested 1992), Nara University of Education (attested 1992), and served as a professor at Osaka University (attested 2016–2017).

Hitoshi Miyake (1933–) is a scholar of religious studies and Japanology. He studied at Keio University (~1951–1955) and the University of Tokyo (~1955–1962), later serving as a professor at Keio University (~1972–1999) and Kokugakuin University (~1999–2004).

Hitoshi Obara (1944–) works in Japanology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Hokkaido University (~1963–1967) and served as a professor at the University of the Sacred Heart from approximately 1989 to 2015.

Hla Pe (1913–2007) was a linguist who studied at the University of Rangoon, UCL, and SOAS. At SOAS University of London, he taught Burmese language and culture beginning in 1948 and served as Professor of Burmese from 1966 to 1980.
Ho-chin Yang is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed a PhD at the University of Washington by 1994, studying under doctoral supervisor Leonard van der Kuijp.

Hojun Nagasaki (1934–) is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara. He was president of the Jaina Studies Society in 1998 and became professor emeritus at Otani University in 1999.
Hokai (1768–1834) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Hōgetsu and Zuihe.
Hokei Izumi (1884–1947) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Otani University and later served there as a professor, attested in 1930.

Holly Gayley is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed doctoral studies in Tibetan and Himalayan Studies at Harvard University (~2002–2009) and held a post at the University of Colorado around 2008.

Holmes Welch (1924–1981) worked in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He studied at Harvard University (~1940–1957) under Francis Woodman Cleaves, and later served as a lecturer at both Harvard University and Yale University.

Hong Luo works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. A former doctoral student at Peking University, Luo has held posts at the China Tibetology Research Center and as a professor at Sichuan University.

Hongyue Guo is a scholar in Sinology and Buddhist studies. Guo studied under teacher Xubang Qi and completed a PhD at Indiana University under doctoral supervisor Stephen R. Bokenkamp, attested in 2007.

Honsho Ueda (1937–) is a Buddhist studies scholar. He served as a lecturer (attested 1963) and professor (attested 1992) at Minobusan Junior College, professor at Minobusan University (attested 1996), and director of the Institute for Advanced Studies on Asia (attested 1996).
Hoong Teik Toh works in Tibetology, Sinology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Gray Tuttle, Ruohong Li, and Yudru Tsomu, completing a PhD at Harvard University by 2004.
